_register: Brazilian software addresses the reader with « você » (never « tu », never « o senhor/a senhora ») in sentences, in a polite but plain tone; buttons, menu entries and step lists use the infinitive (Emprestar, Salvar, Ler o código de barras); no jokes, no exclamation marks; no gender-neutral forms with @, x or e (write « aluno », « professor »).
_quotes: Curly double quotes “text” (U+201C, U+201D), nested quotes ‘ ’; no space before : ; ? ! or inside the quotes (e.g. Emprestado: “{{title}}”); Brazilian number format (decimal comma, thousands dot) and dates dd/mm/aaaa; the arrow → stays; Brazilian spelling after the 1990 agreement (« ação », « ótimo », no « Pt-PT » forms such as « ecrã » or « utilizador »).
_plural: Two forms are enough (one, other); in Brazilian Portuguese « one » covers 0 and 1 (« 0 aluno », « 1 aluno », « 2 alunos »), so write messages that read naturally with « one » for zero as well.

copy.note: One physical copy with its own barcode; never « cópia » (that is a photocopy or a backup copy).

record.note: Bibliographic record, as in Koha pt-BR and Brazilian cataloguing (MARC, « registro bibliográfico »); « ficha » is the old card catalogue and is not used.

patron.note: The standard word of Brazilian library science, Pergamum and Koha pt-BR; « leitor » is also used in schools but clashes with the barcode reader. Staff logins are never called « usuário »: use « conta ».

card.note: Everyday Brazilian word for the library card; « cartão de usuário » is the formal equivalent. Keep one: « carteirinha ».

return.note: The action: « Devolução » on the menu, « devolver » or « registrar a devolução » for the verb.

renew.note: Standard word in Brazilian libraries for extending the due date.

due date.note: Short form of « data prevista de devolução »; « prazo » only for the length of the period.

overdue.note: « atrasado » for a single adjective (empréstimo atrasado).

reminder.note: The printed slip asking for the return; « cobrança » sounds like a debt and is not used.

call number.note: The shelf mark on the spine (B 4 DEL, 590 ROS), as in Brazilian libraries; « localização » and « cota » are not used.

spine band.note: The coloured band with pictogram and call number on the spine; « lombada » alone is the spine.

class.note: A school class (3 B); « classe » means social class or a grammatical class in Brazil, so it is not used.

group.note: Used for a group of teachers.

genre.note: Brazilian spelling with the circumflex (not « género »).

classification.note: The sorting scheme (CDD, Dewey, for non-fiction).

catalogue.note: Written « catálogo »; « acervo » is the collection as a whole and is used only where the text means all the holdings.

stocktaking.note: Checking the shelves against the catalogue; « inventário » is the usual word in Brazilian libraries for the shelf check (« conferência do acervo » is a descriptive alternative, not used as a title).

wish list.note: Books a patron would like the library to have; « desiderata » is the librarians' technical word but less plain, « lista de desejos » sounds like an online shop.

census.note: Registering the usuários with their photo; « recenseamento » is the literal word but is understood as a national census.

class upgrade.note: Moving every class up a year at the end of the school year (3 B becomes 4 B).

staff account.note: A shared login per role; « equipe » (Brazilian spelling), not « pessoal » and not « usuário ».

backup.note: The loanword is the everyday word in Brazil; « cópia de segurança » is correct but less used, keep « backup » everywhere. Plural « backups ».

colour set.note: Written « cores »; « paleta » for the interface palette.

scanner.note: The USB barcode reader that types like a keyboard; this is the usual Brazilian name. Short form « leitor » only where the context is clear; it does not clash because the patron is « usuário ».

student.note: Feminine « aluna » only where the gender is known; the plain form is « aluno ».

teacher.note: Feminine « professora » only where the gender is known; the plain form is « professor ».

school year.note: Brazilian term; « ano escolar » refers to the grade a student is in.

note.note: A staff note in the Notes area; « nota » means a grade or a banknote in Brazilian school contexts, so it is avoided.

return desk / circulation desk.note: The desk where loans and returns are handled; the area as a whole is « Empréstimos ».
